entries.subject: Nathan, Head and Huber (2024), deblurred imagery and geologic mapping
entries.finding: Excluded as a direct mapped replacement. Appendix p. 9 explicitly states that the workflow discards geospatial information and requires registration to another map. The supporting data are paper figures/tables and a processing tutorial; a qualified registered raster was not identified. A future re-registration could improve visual interpretation.
entries.revisitWhen: A Titania source release provides the missing downloadable mapped data, projection, measured quantity and coverage for direct comparison with the selected inputs.

entries.subject: PDS OPUS Voyager frames, including vg-iss-2-u-c2683649 used by Nathan et al.
entries.finding: Authoritative acquisition archive; selected LPI products already provide controlled mosaicking and DEMs. Reprocessing individual images requires its own calibration/registration evidence.

entries.subject: NASA color composite
entries.finding: Useful visual reference, excluded as a map dataset: a published disc composite does not establish registered global color coverage.
entries.revisitWhen: A Titania observation or controlled reconstruction demonstrates useful native surface detail, body-fixed geometry and independent registration beyond the cited sampling or coverage limits.

entries.subject: USGS Gazetteer
entries.finding: Coordinate and nomenclature reference, not a separate observation dataset. Named sample locations also appear in Nathan et al. Table A1.

entries.subject: Thomson and Baynham (2026) historical geology
entries.finding: The CC BY 4.0 release supplies ten historical Voyager-era polygon units. Its incompatible Earth CRS is reconstructed from six crater centroids with four independent crater checks, differing by 0.33–0.83 degrees (about 4.5–11.4 km). Categorical coverage is about 35.3%; source holes and unsupported overlap order remain missing. This is mapped interpretation, not measured composition or terrain, and the check differences are not universal boundary uncertainties.

entries.subject: Voyager 2 ISS green/violet/ultraviolet color frames
entries.finding: 17 GEOMED frames in 6 complete sets (7.4 to 24.4 km per pixel) placed by limb fit and mosaic registration supply the Voyager color dataset. Whole-disc violet/green and ultraviolet/green are tied to Bell and McCord (1991) Fig. 2 (0.96, 0.92); the archive calibration gives 0.830 and 0.912. No phase normalisation; the north stays unavailable.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Hapke law of Veverka et al. (1987), read in the table Verbiscer and Veverka print in NASA's Reports of Planetary Geology and Geophysics Program 1987 (TM-4041, page 181); the paper itself was not read. Titania's row: w = 0.48, h = 0.018, S(0) = 0.77, roughness 23 degrees, g = -0.28, Hapke's 1986 equation. The model here takes the opposition amplitude B0, so S(0) is converted with the authors' definition, B0 = S(0)/(w P(0)), printed in the 1986 report: B0 = 0.65. Flood-lit, the limb is 0.97 of the centre; the narrow opposition surge puts the point under the Sun at 0.70 of that centre at 10 degrees phase. It is second class twice over: the fit is to whole-disc photometry, taken as a limb law because the same group reports that whole-disc and disc-resolved fits agree excellently for Titania (TM-4130, page 238, citing Thomas et al. 1987); and neither range is printed. The phase range 0.8 to 152.6 degrees is the span of the resolved Voyager 2 frames the PDS node lists, and the emission limit 86.2 degrees comes from the outermost pixel of the finest whole-disc clear frame (C2684315, 3.403 km per pixel); both are derived here. Thomas and Veverka's 1986 summary gives a Minnaert k near 0.7 at 33 degrees phase, one phase only. Helfenstein, Veverka and Thomas (1988) could not be read.
entries.revisitWhen: The disc-resolved fit of Thomas et al. (1987), with its ranges, is read in the paper.

entries.subject: Shared sphere bank lighting (Lambert with a 0.35 flood floor and 0.05 ambient term, adapted from OpenSpace)
entries.finding: Replaced by the Hapke law of Veverka et al. (1987); Titania now bakes its own bank.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Surface map left edge after the raster lane change
entries.finding: The raster lane writes this map from 0° E, but surface-map.json still declared the retired atlas's 180° E left edge, so the globe, labels and status-bar longitude were half a turn from the imagery. Read through its georeferenced source, the prepared normal map correlates 0.87 from 0° E and 0.16 from 180° E. The declaration is now 0° E, and preparation refuses a declared edge the source contradicts.
